material_language: CRT or LCD glass plate glare caught on a side-lit slab
compressed GIF edge shimmer translated into physical banding
black toner dust and photocopy burn
cut plastic or enamel product-shell surface
lighting: Side-lit and contrast-heavy: a hard grazing light should reveal the slab thickness, dither relief, dust, scratches, and glassy burn. Keep the background dim-to-gray rather than pure black so the rupture has volume; let source apertures provide the brightest points.
object_inventory: One major impossible-scale dither object should dominate, cropped beyond the plate edge, with one secondary fracture path and 6 to 10 small source-bearing interruptions nested into its cuts, chips, seams, and glints.

The Dither Boy anchor should appear as the governing surface language, not a literal product screenshot: the entire plate behaves like a physicalized dithering engine. Supporting sources become real marks along the rupture: noir as high-contrast film chip, hacking as hidden terminal-glow notch, music-as-software as a narrow pulsing seam, web literature as a tiny live page aperture, Detroit/autonomous forest as quieter edge cuts with image or texture evidence.
negative_constraints: no equal-weight grid of source objects
no unrelated replacement image or metaphorical scene when a source image is attached
flat sleeve or polite material scan
generic torn poster wall without source-paper evidence
do not strip handmade details into generic torn-paper ambience
do not fragment the primary source objects until their original silhouettes stop reading
do not replace source candy/wrapper/handwriting cues with unrelated scraps
